newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq shows its biggest point gain as techs surge.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq shows its biggest point gain as techs surge.

text.p: A stunning rally in technology stocks pushed Nasdaq shares up nearly 35 points on Friday in the largest single-session point gain ever.

The Nasdaq composite index ended a weeklong rally at 1305.37, up 34.87 points, or 2.74 percent. The point gain tops the previous record gain of 33.18 points on July 17, 1996. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners 2787 to 1443 on total volume of 692 million shares.
The Nasdaq outpaced the Dow industrials, which gained nearly 95 points, or 1.36 percent, to close unofficially at 7071.

"The semiconductor stocks were just blistering today. Everything got a lift, but people were really looking for stocks that were even lower than low that were ripe to buy," said Richard Whittington, a SoundView Financial Group analyst.
The strength in technology stocks spread across several sectors, lifting shares of computer makers, semiconductor developers and networking companies, traders said.
The surge solidified market leaders Intel Corp and Dell Computer Corp and boosted smaller capitalization stocks such as Lam Research Corp and VLSI Technology Inc.
